The hostile gauntlet

Twenty-six LTC files, each broken one way on purpose, with an answer key. Two readers took it: GoButton's own reader (the ltc.js the show runs, untouched) and a careful reader, the same code with three changes. Both are told nothing: no frame rate, no polarity, no speed.

297 wrong frames from GoButton's reader across the files and the sweeps  ·  0 from the careful reader. Files passed: 22 and 22 of 26.

A wrong frame is the worst thing a reader can do: a lighting desk that hears no timecode waits, but one that hears the wrong time jumps the show. LTC has no checksum. It has two checks a reader can make for free: the polarity bit keeps every frame's count of 0s even, and every frame is the one after the frame before. GoButton's reader makes neither.

The careful reader's three changes

Listen with hysteresis. A flip counts only when the signal crosses a band a fifth of its height wide, centred on its own middle. Noise 10 dB down: 64% read and 26 wrong becomes 94% and none. The cost: through a 1.2 kHz low-pass the 1s no longer reach the band and the reader goes deaf, where GoButton's still reads. Wider bands read more noise and less smear; there is no free width.

A gap is a gap. A pulse over four bits long is silence, not a new measure of the bit: forget the measure and learn it again.

Trust only a checked frame. Even 0s, and the frame after the last. On the EQ file GoButton's reader found every sync word and read 119 frames, all wrong; the careful reader passed on none. Silence beat a lie. It costs one frame of delay at every lock.

Still open

Noise 6 dB down, MP3 at 32 kbps and the resonant EQ defeat both readers; a reader that times its crossings through a filter matched to the bit, rather than the raw zero, should take them. And backward: GoButton's reader is forward-only, so 23-reverse waits for the room's backward reader to join the gauntlet.
